messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Elevated 5xx + latency for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in us-west-2 (potential AWS control plane / auth dependency). See AWS status: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ — auto-page to on-call.
Alex G: saw alert spike 06:14 UTC. multiple customers reporting timeouts and 5xx on token exchange and inference requests.
Marta L: acked. I'm on it — looking at api-gateway / auth proxy traces now.
Marta L: quick snippet from proxy logs (us-west-2):
```
2026-03-15T06:13:58Z auth-proxy us-west-2 ERROR upstream=STS 503 duration=231ms request_id=abc123
2026-03-15T06:14:02Z proxy us-west-2 WARN retrying token fetch -> 3/3
2026-03-15T06:14:03Z public-api us-west-2 ERROR handler panic: downstream auth 5xx
```
Alex G: looks like STS/iam/control-plane timeouts — downstream token fetch failures causing request path 500s. Confirmed also increased API latency in load tests.
Oncall Pager: paging @marta @alexg @samk. Can we activate region-fallback routing?
Marta L: yes, pushing region-fallback policy to route non-sensitive traffic to eu-west-1 for hosted endpoints. Will exclude Dedicated pools with strict data locality.
Sam K: I'm taking Dedicated on-call. For dedicated pools in us-west-2, nodes are experiencing long KV-cache eviction times because instance metadata calls time out. Mitigation options: 1) enable aggressive local caching of STS tokens, 2) increase retry backoff, 3) temporarily drain user traffic to other regions if allowed.
Emily R: CS reporting high-severity for 4 enterprise customers — visible 5xx on their integrations. CS Lead, want me to open customer-facing incident notes?
CS Lead: yes, please post a short status page update and include expected impact. Customers affected: Acme, Stripe-like Corp, FinApp. Note: some Dedicated customers in us-west-2 with pinned capacity are impacted.
Marta L: executing mitigation: enabling token-cache TTL bump and switching hosted non-PII routes to eu-west-1 (gradual rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Command I'm running:
```bash
# update routing policy
redwood-cli routes set --name hosted --region-fallback eu-west-1 --percent 10 --reason "aws us-west-2 control-plane errors"
```
Infra Bot: autoscaler observed queue backlog in us-west-2 dedicated pools + increased replica churn. Triggered soft-quarantine on two nodes.
Marta L: quarantined nodes reaped, scaling new instances in eu-west-1 for hosted traffic. Meanwhile Sam, please validate Dedicated fallback plan with product and security.
Sam K: confirmed with product/security — cannot cross-region Dedicated customer data without approval. For those, we're applying local mitigations: increase token cache TTL, reduce internal metadata calls, and throttle worker concurrency to reduce pressure. Rolling patch now to prod-dedicated-agent.
Alex G: metrics summary so far: 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 7.6% for hosted in us-west-2; median latency +420ms. Dedicated pool error rate up to 4.9% for impacted zones.
Oncall Pager: current incident severity P1. Escalating to SRE lead @emily. Please add to bridge: https://meet.redwood.inc/bridges/1773001234
Emily R: on bridge. Looking at vendor feed — AWS console shows partial control plane issues in us-west-2 affecting IAM/STS and EC2 metadata endpoints. Link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/USW2-2026-03
Marta L: handoff: I'm stepping out in 35m for scheduled offshift. Sam, you're on the next rotation — handing over draft postmortem notes and runbook pointers.
Sam K: taking handoff. Action items I'm owning: 1) finalize customer communication (CS), 2) push durable token-cache change to Dedicated nodes, 3) prepare rollback plan for region-fallback if we see error propagation.
Marta L: runbook refs: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/aws-region-controlplane-outage and https://internal.redwood/ops/region-fallback-playbook
Alex G: quick rollback snippet if region fallback causes regressions:
```bash
redwood-cli routes set --name hosted --region-fallback none --reason "rollback - observed increased latency on eu-west-1" --percent 0
```
Infra Bot: note — CloudWatch alarm cw-queue-usw2 breached 3x in last 10m, and we auto-suspended non-critical background jobs in us-west-2 to reduce pressure.
CS Lead: drafted customer note posted to status.redwood.com (please review): "We are experiencing elevated errors and latency for API requests in us-west-2 due to third-party (AWS) control plane issues. We have implemented partial routing to eu-west-1 for non-sensitive traffic and are applying localized mitigations for Dedicated customers. Engineers are actively investigating. Updates every 30 minutes."
Oncall Pager: next update scheduled +30m. Sam, please own until resolved or until you hand off. Marta, thanks for the initial triage. :thumbsup:
Sam K: acknowledged. Leaving bridge pinned and monitoring dashboards. If AWS confirms full resolution, we'll run post-fix validation: synthetic test suite across endpoints + k6 smoke tests, then revert region-fallback.
Emily R: adding post-incident tasks: add stricter caching for metadata/sts calls to runtime, improve fallback automation to allow per-customer policies, and add an observability alert for third-party control-plane 5xx correlation.
Incident Bot: Incident update logged. Severity=P1. Thread will be referenced in postmortem.
Sam K: will publish interim incident note in 1h, and convene triage for root cause once stable.
CS Lead: confirming customer comms and CS reps on standby for elevated tickets.
Marta L: leaving handoff: all playbooks + ssh keys in bridge. Good luck team.
Sam K: thanks — taking over.
_meta: generated for dataset realism: incident coordination for aws us-west-2 control plane degradation affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools
